title: Sampling new names
objectives: Write a sampler that draws names letter by letter from a model with a seeded generator.

screens.title: Two writers
screens.prose: Two models each write six names, both drawn with seed 3. One is the bigram of level 1; the other is the MLP of level 2.

options.text: No way to tell: both are random

naelynn and zakynel against n and ilemiyanic.

byKey.a: You picked the list with n and ilemiyanic. A one-letter memory cannot keep a name’s shape.

c starts at the running total 0.8; 0.62 is below it.

0.62 is above 0.5 and below 0.8.

screens.title: A name by hand
screens.prose: Name the rule: the **sampling rule** takes the first running total strictly above $u$; in NumPy, `np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(p), u, side="right")`. Start from three marks, draw, append, slide the context, and stop at the end mark.

state.caption: A planted model over ., a, b and c: each row gives the chances of the next symbol.

screens.question: Draw a name from the planted model with $u$ = 0.62, 0.35, 0.40, 0.15 in turn. Fill in the symbol each $u$ picks.

After a, the running totals are 0.4, 0.5, 0.8, 1.
b, then a, then a (0.40 equals the total 0.4, so it is past end), then end: baa.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Each draw uses the row of the symbol just drawn.

screens.question: You run the sampler twice with seed 7 and once with seed 8. What do you get?

options.why: A seed fixes the whole stream of u, so the same seed repeats exactly.
A different seed gives a different stream, so seed 8 writes other names.

hints.text: What does a seed fix?
The stream of u values, and so every draw.

feedback.correct: Same seed, same names: runs can be checked and repeated.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what the seed controls.

explain.text: The seed fixes every $u$, and the rule turns each $u$ into one symbol, so seed 7 repeats exactly. That is what lets a test check a sampler’s names letter by letter.

The most likely names, in order
options.why: Argmax at each step gives one path, not a list; and it need not be the most likely name.

No: from `...` it always follows the same path, alee.

screens.prose: The sampler stops after 20 letters even without the end mark. Of the MLP’s 500 names, 2 hit that cap.

screens.question: Why cap the length at all?

options.why: Real names reach 15 letters; the cap only guards against a run that never ends.
It makes a bad run finish; it does not speed up a good one.

hints.text: What if the end mark’s chance is tiny?
A run could go on and on; a cap ends it.

feedback.correct: Without a cap, a model that rarely ends could run for ever.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Think of a model that never picks the end mark.

explain.text: The longest real name has 15 letters, so 20 never cuts a real-looking name short. A half-trained or planted model may hardly ever pick the end mark, and the cap keeps the sampler finite.

screens.title: A u on the edge
screens.prose: Running totals in floats need not reach exactly 1: ten chances of 0.1 add to `0.9999999999999999`, and `rng.random()` can return that very number.
screens.question: For $u$ equal to the last running total, `0.9999999999999999`, what does `searchsorted(..., side="right")` return for 27 symbols?

options.text: 27: past the end, so cap it

options.why: No total is strictly above u, so it returns the length, 27.
It searches upward; it never wraps to the start.

hints.text: Is any running total strictly above u?
None is, so the answer is the length of the list.

feedback.correct: 27: cap it at 26 so the draw stays a real symbol.
feedback.generic: Not quite. side="right" returns the first position whose total is above u.

byKey.26: You expected the last symbol. With no total above u, searchsorted returns the length, 27.

explain.text: With no total strictly above $u$, `searchsorted` returns the length, 27, which is no symbol. Capping at 26 gives the last letter, z, the stretch that rounding cut off.

widget.solution:
import numpy as np

SYMBOLS = ".abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"


def sample_name(prob_fn, rng, max_len=20):
    context = [0, 0, 0]
    name = ""
    while len(name) < max_len:
        p = prob_fn(context)
        u = rng.random()
        ix = min(int(np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(p), u, side="right")), 26)
        if ix == 0:
            break
        name += SYMBOLS[ix]
        context = context[1:] + [ix]
    return name
widget.how: Submit runs 5 hidden tests: fixed u values on the planted model (one u equals a running total), and three seeds on it. Then come a model that never ends (the cap), a u equal to the last running total (the cap at 26), and one name from the trained MLP with seed 7. `toy`, `only_a`, `tenths`, `mlp` and `FixedU` are ready.

screens.title: Synthetic price paths
screens.prose: A risk desk fits a model to ten years of daily returns and samples 10,000 synthetic paths for a stress test. A reviewer finds that many sampled paths repeat whole months of real history.
screens.question: What should the desk check?

options.text: Nothing: copies of real months are realistic
options.why: A stress test needs new paths; a model that replays history says nothing about what has not happened.

options.text: Change the seed until the copies go away
options.why: A seed changes which paths are drawn, not what the model learned.

hints.text: What did 19.4% measure for names?
The share of samples that are training data.

feedback.correct: Measure the share of copies, as with names, and treat a high share as memorising.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Recall what the 500-name check measured.

byKey.seed: Re-seeding hides the copies in one run; the model would still be replaying history.

explain.text: A generator that mostly replays its training data adds little to a stress test. The names check carries over: sample many, count exact copies, and compare with what a good model should repeat.

ideas: Lay the chances end to end and draw $u$: the symbol is the first running total strictly above $u$, `searchsorted(cumsum(p), u, side="right")`, capped at 26.
Start from `...`, draw, append, slide the context, stop at the end mark or after 20 letters. A seed fixes every draw.
Taking the top symbol each step writes one name for ever (alee); 19.4% of the MLP’s draws are training names, most are new.

formula.name: Sampling rule
formula.tex: i = \min\big(\#\{k : c_k \le u\},\ 26\big), \quad c_k = \textstyle\sum_{j \le k} p_j
formula.note: $u$ from `rng.random()`; equal to a total, it goes to the next symbol.

summary.trap: Taking the most likely symbol every step instead of drawing, which writes one name for ever.
